heading: Assertion heads
text:
### Assertion heads [LTSL.8.2]

Each head is a past-tense observation the compiler lowers to one `Oracle*` oracle atom
([RDSC.7.1], [RLOW.17.1]):

| Head | Asserts | Atom |
|---|---|---|
| `activated <rule>` | the rule produced and ran an activation | `OracleActivated` |
| `emitted <Schema> …` | an `emit` of a matching fact | `OracleEmit` |
| `published <Schema> …` | a `publish` of a matching fact | `OraclePublish` |
| `called <service> [as "corr"]` | an outbound call to the service (optionally a correlation) | `OracleCall` |
| `cached "k" [: v]` | a cache write of `k` (optionally value `v`) | `OracleCacheSet` |
| `cache_deleted "k"` | a cache delete of `k` | `OracleCacheDelete` |
| `logged <level> ["substr"]` | a `log` at that level (optionally matching a substring) | `OracleLog` |
| `retracted <Schema> …` | a matching fact left working memory | `OracleRetract` |
| `wm has <Schema> …` / `wm count <Schema> == N` / `wm empty` | working-memory state at end of run | `OracleWorkingMemory` |

A subset-matching head (`emitted` / `published` / `retracted` / `wm has`) matches
a schema-typed fact by **subset slot equality** — the given slots must equal the
observed fact's, other slots free — over exact values ([LTSL.4.3]). The one
non-schema value is the `cached "k": v` cache value, **opaque JSON**, which
matches `v` as two JSON values do ([LTSL.4.3]).

`recorded` is not a head: the compiler must reject it
(`DS_VALIDATE_TEST_RECORDED_RETIRED`) with a message naming `called`, the head
that asserts a call.
